components.evidence: PE32/PE32+ mapping, relocations and normal imports are tested. Exports, name/ordinal lookup, forwarded exports with bounded depth and cycle detection, runtime-to-runtime import binding, and the PE32 TLS directory plus a process/thread TLS owner with callback plans are implemented and host-tested; delay imports remain.
Wine modules have an explicit runtime origin; POSIX and PS5 providers keep independently configured application/runtime roots, covered by host tests.

The first PE32 title is playable on FW 12.02 with exact host parity and bounded hardware evidence. For Wine, the translator now also covers FS-prefixed absolute dword operands, LOCK-prefixed group-1 memory read-modify-write, BT/BTS/BTR/BTC, CMOVcc, the SSE data-movement/lane slice (movd/movq/movdqa/movdqu/movups/movaps/movss/movsd, punpck/packss, pshufd and friends, pextrw/pinsrw) and BSF/BSR, each with architectural tests and residency/lazy-flag parity where the form allows it. With the Unix-call bridge enabled, real ntdll initialization now retires 8577 instructions, services three NtAllocateVirtualMemory calls and maps 88 KiB of guest memory before meeting the next untranslated family.
Synthetic integer call bridge exists; imports, callbacks, FP/vector arguments and exception transitions remain.

The pinned revision 490f6d5d builds a reproducible i386 PE runtime (two clean builds byte-identical, recorded in a validated manifest) and a bounded host gate maps it from PW_FILE_RUNTIME, binds kernelbase's 428 imports against ntdll's exports and executes ntdll's exported NtClose stub through the DBT until the first Unix-call boundary. No Windows process starts yet and no title uses it: process initialization, kernelbase load under a real process and Wine test smoke runs remain.

The dispatcher boundary is located in the built image (exported __wine_syscall_dispatcher slot plus the single jmp-dword-ptr thunk that references it) and the call number is re-read from the issuing stub inside the mapped image. A versioned table of the pinned i386 syscall numbers, names and argument widths is cross-checked against the Wine source; the two-level stub frame is unwound correctly; and NtAllocateVirtualMemory is serviced for the first-boot profile with guest pointers validated through the dispatcher's own region check, so real ntdll initialization proceeds past its first two calls before meeting an unimplemented instruction family. Remaining: every other call, reserve/commit distinction, nested calls and rollback of a partially failed handler.

One guest thread has isolated CPU/FP/FS state. PE32 TLS now has a process/thread owner: stable module indices published through mapped guest memory, per-thread template-plus-zero-fill storage from a caller-owned arena, guest FS:[0x2C] lookup and deterministic attach/detach callback plans driven by the DBT's guest-callback mechanism, with two-thread and rollback coverage. The Wine gate additionally owns a minimal guest TEB (FS base, StackBase, StackLimit, Self, ProcessEnvironmentBlock) and a zeroed PEB so real ntdll initialization can run. Real PEB/PEB_LDR_DATA construction, module entry-point ordering and native thread adapters remain.
No general Wine-compatible object/handle or WaitForMultipleObjects service is claimed.
Low-address reserve/commit/protect/release and W^X DBT publication are validated for the current profile.
Precise DBT faults exist, but PE32 SEH dispatch/unwind and Wine context delivery do not.
Title-confined read/seek and INI access exist; NT paths, directories, sharing, async I/O and file objects remain.
A bounded persistent registry and CP1252 bootstrap exist; Wine registry views, environment and Unicode/NLS remain.
WinMM PCM and DualSense-to-message adapters are hardware validated for one title.
No Winsock compatibility surface is claimed.
DXVK is the selected D3D8/9/10/11 path; it has not started on PS5.
The companion project renders and computes on gfx1013 but does not yet satisfy its pinned DXVK consumer profile.
ps5log/1 identity, runtime counters and ordered close/relaunch are hardware validated.
